column2: The Pretoria Settlement: Authority of the Crown

The campaign has ended in Britain's favour, and the delegates at Pretoria must decide how victory will be translated into government. Boer representatives seek to preserve district institutions and protect communities exhausted by the fighting, imperial officials insist that the republic can no longer conduct an independent foreign policy. A separate British Transvaal administration would retain those institutions under Crown supervision. If Transvaal possesses eastern districts in South Mozambique, Britain can instead detach them for direct administration while keeping an inland dependency. The strongest demand would abolish the separate government altogether, bringing its remaining territory under colonial rule at the cost of greater resistance and administrative expense. The choice determines both the boundaries of the settlement and the responsibilities that follow it.
Preserve British Transvaal as a separate Crown dependency.
